text:
kevin.perf: Heads up — after the kernel-selector tweak landed yesterday, we're seeing host-side parse + proto marshalling regression on short responses. p99 up ~8-12ms on 64B-ish payloads.

maria.runtime: ugh. is that on both http/gRPC?

kevin.perf: mostly gRPC paths so far. http has noise but smaller. repro harness: 10k qps small request test. baseline (pre-change) p99 decode+parse ~6ms, now ~18ms.

liz.dev: any flamegraphs or perf entries?

kevin.perf: attaching quick run output:

```
# perf top sampling during p99 storm
- runtime::proto::marshal     32.4%
- runtime::ingress::parse     18.6%
- net::grpc::writev           12.1%
- small_allocs                9.2%
- memcpy                      7.8%
```

kevin.perf: pprof CPU shows proto marshalling split into multiple memcpy hotspots (small copies per field) when kernel selection picks the avx-fallback path.

maria.runtime: kernel-selector change — was supposed to favor vectorized kernels for long sequences. Could it be falling back unexpectedly for short seqs and causing extra temp buffers?

aj.sre: we also saw kvcache miss rate tick up during the same window on dedicated hosts. possible correlation: more memory churn -> cache spills -> extra parse work?

kevin.perf: good call. I sampled kvcache stats during the run: eviction rate spiked ~3x. net effect: more prefix fetches -> more small parse calls.

liz.dev: quick reproduction steps I used locally:

1) set AUTOBATCH_MAX_WINDOW_MS=2 (production default was 5 before change)
2) run small-req harness: ./tools/miniload --model small --qps 10k --seq 8

I noticed when window is small we flush more often and proto marshaller gets many short lifetimes -> allocator churn.

maria.runtime: so two orthogonal levers: kernel-selection (vector vs fallback) and batching window. Could be interacting: selector chooses kernel based on observed batch sizes; smaller windows -> smaller batches -> fallback path -> more mem ops.

kevin.perf: yup. hypothesis: kernel_selector now samples an exponent-weighted seq distribution; for microbursts it underestimates tail and picks the slower codepath for short batches.

aj.sre: any immediate mitigation we can roll? revert kernel-selector tweak or bump autobatch window?

maria.runtime: quick mitigation plan: 1) pin kernel selection policy for short sequences to legacy path (cheap memcpy-friendly kernel) 2) increase minimal batch window to 4ms for gRPC ingress 3) add kvcache-adaptive hysteresis to avoid spill loops.

kevin.perf: I bench-mapped a microfix: forcing legacy kernel for seq<=16 reduces p99 back to ~7ms in the harness.

liz.dev: plz share the patch, I'll run CI perf. Also let's add a small microbenchmark test that simulates ~200B serialized proto objects to catch regressions in marshalling.

maria.runtime: agreed. I'll open an RFC to add the microbenchmark to perf CI and a quick rollback-guard on selector.

deploy-bot: deploy 1768 -> canary started on rtm-hostpool-7 (4 hosts).

aj.sre: watching canary kvcache eviction now. if eviction goes above 1.5x baseline for 5m we rollback.

kevin.perf: follow-ups: I'll instrument marshaller to aggregate tiny-copy counts (per-request) and emit metric runtime.proto.small_copy_count. If that spikes we can trigger selector fallback.

liz.dev: note: also look at grpc writev pattern — observed many 6-8 small write calls per response. batching writev in proxy improves tail a lot. I'll prototype coalescing in the ingress proxy.

maria.runtime: timeline: kevin lands instrumentation PR today, liz pushes writev coalesce prototype, I prepare selector patch + autobatch default tweak. If canary passes we can cut a patch release.

kevin.perf: thanks — posting perf graphs to the thread later. short-term: avoid changing kernel selection heuristics without adding microburst sims to the validation suite. :+1:

aj.sre: looping in @oncall in case canary triggers rollback.

maria.runtime: tagging owners: @liz.dev (proxy), @kevin.perf (perf), @maria.runtime (selector).
